title.zh: 卷一百十五 列傳第五十三: 完顏奴申 崔立 李琦 聶天驥 赤盞尉忻
title.en: Volume 115 Biographies 53: Wanyan Nushen, Cui Li, Li Qi, Nie Tianji, Chizhan Weixin
title.raw: 卷一百十五 列傳第五十三: 完顏奴申 崔立 李琦 聶天驥 赤盞尉忻 Volume 115 Biographies 53: Wanyan Nushen, Cui Li, Li Qi, Nie Tianji, Chizhan Weixin

sentences.zh: 完顏奴申

translations.literal: Wanyan Nushen
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Nushen

sentences.zh: 完顏奴申，字正甫，素蘭之弟也。

translations.literal: Wanyan Nushen, courtesy name Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Sulan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Nushen, whose courtesy name was Zhengfu, was the younger brother of Sulan.

sentences.zh: 登策論進士第，仕曆清要。

translations.literal: He passed the Policy Essays jinshi examination and served in posts of clear importance.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Policy Essays and rose through posts of high standing.

sentences.zh: 正大三年八月，由翰林直學士充益政院說書官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhengda, from Hanlin Direct Academician he was appointed Lecturer at the Beneficial Governance Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhengda 3 (1226), having served as Hanlin Direct Academician, he was made lecturer at the Beneficial Governance Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1228), he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 監察御史烏古論石魯剌劾近侍張文壽、仁壽、李麟之受敵帥饋遺，詔奴申鞫問，得其奸狀，上曲赦其罪，皆斥去，朝論快之。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wugulun Shilula impeached the close attendants Zhang Wenshou, Renshou, and Li Linzhi for receiving gifts from the enemy commander; the emperor ordered Nushen to investigate, and when their treachery was established, the emperor bent the law to pardon them, yet all were dismissed, to the satisfaction of court opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Censor Wugulun Shilula impeached the emperor's close attendants Zhang Wenshou, Renshou, and Li Linzhi for accepting gifts from the enemy commander, the court ordered Nushen to investigate. He proved their guilt, but the emperor leniently pardoned them and merely dismissed them all—still, public opinion welcomed the outcome.

sentences.zh: 九月，改侍講學士，以御史大夫奉使大元。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was changed to Academician Lecturer and, as Censor-in-Chief, was sent on embassy to Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made Academician Lecturer and, bearing the title Censor-in-Chief, was dispatched on embassy to the Great Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至龍駒河，朝見太宗皇帝。

translations.literal: He reached the Longju River and had audience with Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the Longju River and had audience with Emperor Taizong of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，還。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，遷吏部尚書，複往。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel and went again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year he was promoted to Minister of Personnel and sent on embassy again.

sentences.zh: 八年春，還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year (1231) he returned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以勞拜參知政事。

translations.literal: The court, in recognition of his labors, appointed him Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his service, the court appointed him Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 天興元年春，大兵駐鄭州海灘寺，遣使招哀宗降。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tianxing, the great army was stationed at Haichuan Temple in Zhengzhou and sent envoys to summon the Emperor Aizong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianxing 1 (1232), the main Mongol force camped at Haichuan Temple in Zhengzhou and sent envoys urging Emperor Aizong to surrender.

sentences.zh: 複以奴申往乞和。

translations.literal: Again Nushen was sent to beg for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen was again sent to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 不許，攻汴益急。

translations.literal: They did not consent, and the attack on Bian grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: They refused, and the assault on Bianjing intensified.

sentences.zh: 汴受圍數月，倉庫匱乏，召武仙等入援不至，哀宗懼，以曹王訛可出質，請罷攻。

translations.literal: Bian had been besieged for months; the storehouses were exhausted; summons to Wu Xian and others to enter in relief did not arrive; the Emperor Aizong was afraid and sent Prince Cao Eke as hostage to request a halt to the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjing had been under siege for months. The granaries were empty, and calls for Wu Xian and others to march to the rescue went unanswered. In fear, Emperor Aizong sent Prince Cao Eke as a hostage and pleaded for the siege to be lifted.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，哀宗議親出捍禦，以奴申參知政事、兼樞密副使，完顏習捏阿不樞密副使、兼知開封府、權參知政事，總諸軍留守京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Emperor Aizong deliberated going out in person to resist; Nushen was made Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Wanyan Xinie A-bu was Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrent Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture and Acting Vice Grand Councillor, to command all armies and remain to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, as Emperor Aizong considered leading the defense in person, he named Nushen Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Wanyan Xinie A-bu Vice Commissioner, concurrent Administrator of Kaifeng and Acting Vice Grand Councillor, to command all forces and hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 又以翰林學士承旨烏古孫卜吉提控諸王府，同判大睦親府事兼都點檢內族合周管宮掖事，左副點檢完顏阿撒、右副點檢溫敦阿裏副之，戶部尚書完顏珠顆兼裏城四面都總領，御史大夫裴滿阿虎帶兼鎮撫軍民都彈壓，諫議大夫近侍局使行省左右司郎中烏古孫奴申兼知宮省事。

translations.literal: Also Hanlin Academician Expositor Wugusun Buji was put in charge of the princely mansions, Associate Administrator of the Great Muxin Princely Establishment and Chief Inspector of the Inner Clans Hezhou was put in charge of palace affairs, with Left Deputy Inspector Wanyan Asa and Right Deputy Inspector Wendun Ali assisting; Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke was made overall commander of the four sides of the inner city; Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai was made overall pacifier and military-civilian suppressor; Remonstrating Censor and Director of the Close Attendants Bureau, Left and Right Bureau Director of the Branch Secretariat Wugusun Nushen was made concurrent Administrator of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also assigned Hanlin Expositor Wugusun Buji to oversee the princely establishments; made Hezhou, Associate of the Great Muxin House and Chief Inspector of the Inner Clans, overseer of the palace quarters, with Deputy Inspectors Wanyan Asa and Wendun Ali assisting; put Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke in charge of all four inner-city sectors; made Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai overall pacifier and suppressor of troops and civilians; and made Remonstrating Censor and Director of the Close Attendants Bureau Wugusun Nushen, who also served as Left and Right Bureau Director of the Branch Secretariat, concurrent overseer of palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 又以把撒合為外城東面元帥，術甲咬住南面元帥，崔立西面元帥，孛術魯買奴北面元帥。

translations.literal: Also Basage was made marshal of the eastern outer wall, Shujia Yaozhu of the south, Cui Li of the west, and Boshulu Mainu of the north.
translations.idiomatic: Basage was named marshal of the eastern outer wall, Shujia Yaozhu of the south, Cui Li of the west, and Boshulu Mainu of the north.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，除拜定，以京城付之。

translations.literal: On yiyou day the appointments were fixed and the capital was entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day the appointments were finalized and the capital entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 又以戶部侍郎刁璧為安撫副使，總招撫司，規運京外糧斛。

translations.literal: Also Vice Minister of Revenue Diao Bi was made Deputy Pacification Commissioner, in charge of the Pacification Commission, to plan transport of grain outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Diao Bi was made Deputy Pacification Commissioner to head the Pacification Commission and organize grain shipments from outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 設講議所，受陳言文字，以大理卿納合德輝、戶部尚書仲平、中京副留守愛失等總其事。

translations.literal: A Deliberation Office was established to receive written submissions; the Minister of Justice Nahan Dehui, Minister of Revenue Zhongping, and Deputy Protector of the Central Capital Aishi and others were put in overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: A Deliberation Office was set up to receive written proposals, with Minister of Justice Nahan Dehui, Minister of Revenue Zhongping, Deputy Protector of the Central Capital Aishi, and others directing its work.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛丑，上出京，服絳紗袍，乘馬導從如常儀。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the twelfth month the emperor left the capital, wearing a crimson gauze robe, mounted on horseback with escort as in the usual ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the twelfth month the emperor departed the capital in a crimson gauze robe, riding out with his usual mounted escort.

sentences.zh: 留守官及京城父老從至城外奉辭，有詔撫諭，仍以鞭揖之。

translations.literal: The officials remaining to guard and the elders of the capital followed to outside the walls to take leave; there was an edict to comfort and instruct them, and he still bowed with his whip to them.
translations.idiomatic: The officials left behind and the elders of the capital followed him to the city gate to bid farewell. He issued an edict of reassurance and still bowed to them from horseback with his whip.

sentences.zh: 速不泬聞上已出，復會兵圍汴。

translations.literal: Subutai, hearing that the emperor had already left, again gathered troops to besiege Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Subutai learned the emperor had left the city, he reassembled his forces and renewed the siege of Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 初，上以東面元帥李辛跋扈出怨言，罷為兵部侍郎，將出，密喻奴申等羈縶之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the eastern marshal Li Xin was overbearing and uttered resentful words, the emperor removed him to Vice Minister of War; as he was about to leave, he secretly instructed Nushen and others to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had demoted the eastern marshal Li Xin to Vice Minister of War after he grew arrogant and muttered complaints. Before leaving the capital, the emperor secretly told Nushen and the others to detain him.

sentences.zh: 上既行，奴申等召辛，辛懼，謀欲出降，棄馬逾城而走。

translations.literal: After the emperor had departed, Nushen and the others summoned Xin; Xin was afraid and plotted to surrender, abandoned his horse, climbed over the wall, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor was gone, Nushen and his colleagues summoned Li Xin. Terrified, Xin plotted to defect, abandoned his horse, and fled over the city wall.

sentences.zh: 奴申等遣人追及之，斬於省門。

translations.literal: Nushen and the others sent men in pursuit, caught up with him, and beheaded him at the gate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen sent pursuers who overtook him and executed him at the Secretariat gate.

sentences.zh: 汴民以上親出師，日聽捷報，且以二相持重，幸以無事。

translations.literal: The people of Bian, because the emperor had gone out in person with the army, daily listened for reports of victory, and moreover because the two chancellors held weight, hoped that all would be well.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Bianjing, believing the emperor had led the army out in person, listened daily for news of victory and took comfort in the authority of the two chief ministers, hoping nothing worse would come.

sentences.zh: 俄聞軍敗衛州，蒼黃走歸德，民大恐，以為不救。

translations.literal: Soon they heard that the army had been defeated at Weizhou and fled in panic to Guide; the people were greatly afraid, thinking there would be no rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the army had been routed at Weizhou and the emperor had fled in disarray to Guide. The populace was terrified, convinced the capital was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 時汴京內外不通，米升銀二兩。

translations.literal: At that time inside and outside Bianjing there was no communication; a sheng of rice cost two taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjing was cut off inside and out; a sheng of rice sold for two taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 百姓糧盡，殍者相望，縉紳士女多行乞於市，至有自食其妻子者，至於諸皮器物皆煮食之，貴家第宅、市樓肆館皆撤以爨。

translations.literal: The common people exhausted their grain; corpses of the starved faced one another; gentry men and women mostly begged in the markets; there were even those who ate their own wives and children; even all leather goods and utensils were boiled and eaten; mansions of great families and market towers and shops were all torn down for fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The people ran out of food; the starved lay one upon another in the streets. Gentlemen and ladies begged in the markets; some ate their own wives and children. Leather goods were boiled for food; mansions, market halls, and shops of the wealthy were torn apart for firewood.

sentences.zh: 及歸德遣使迎兩宮，人情益不安，於是民間有立荊王監國以城歸順之議，而二相皆不知也。

translations.literal: When Guide sent envoys to welcome the two palaces, popular sentiment grew still more uneasy; then among the people there arose talk of establishing Prince Jing as regent and surrendering the city, yet the two chancellors knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Guide sent envoys to fetch the empress dowager and consort, public anxiety deepened. Rumors spread of installing Prince Jing as regent and surrendering the city—but the two chief ministers knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 天興二年正月丙寅，省令史許安國詣講議所言：「古者有大疑，謀及卿士，謀及庶人。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the first month of the second year of Tianxing, Secretariat clerk Xu Anguo went to the Deliberation Office and said: 'In antiquity when there was great doubt, counsel was sought from ministers and nobles and from the common people.'
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the first month of Tianxing 2, Secretariat clerk Xu Anguo addressed the Deliberation Office: 'In antiquity, when grave doubts arose, rulers consulted ministers and commoners alike.'

sentences.zh: 今事勢如此，可集百官及僧道士庶，問保社稷、活生靈之計。

translations.literal: Now that affairs stand thus, we may gather all officials and monks, Daoist priests, and commoners and ask plans to preserve the altars of soil and grain and save the living.
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand at such a pass that we should assemble officials, clergy, and commoners and ask how to preserve the state and save the people.'

sentences.zh: 」左司都事元好問以安國之言白奴申，奴申曰：「此論甚佳，可與副樞議之。

translations.literal: Left Bureau Director Yuan Haowen reported Anguo's words to Nushen; Nushen said: 'This argument is excellent; you may discuss it with the Vice Commissioner.'
translations.idiomatic: Left Bureau Director Yuan Haowen relayed Xu's proposal to Nushen, who replied, 'An excellent idea—discuss it with the Vice Commissioner.'

sentences.zh: 」副樞亦以安國之言為然。

translations.literal: The Vice Commissioner also regarded Anguo's words as right.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Commissioner agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「自車駕出京，今二十日許，又遣使迎兩宮。

translations.literal: Haowen said: 'Since the imperial carriage left the capital, it is now about twenty days, and again envoys have been sent to welcome the two palaces.'
translations.idiomatic: Haowen said, 'It has been some twenty days since the emperor left, and now envoys have been sent to fetch the empress dowager and consort.'

sentences.zh: 民間洶洶，皆謂國家欲棄京城，相公何以處之？

translations.literal: Among the people there is uproar; all say the state intends to abandon the capital—how will you, Chancellor, deal with this?'
translations.idiomatic: The streets are in an uproar; everyone says the court means to abandon the capital. How do you intend to answer this, my lords?'

sentences.zh: 」阿不曰：「吾二人惟有一死耳。

translations.literal: A-bu said: 'We two have only death.'
translations.idiomatic: A-bu said, 'For us two, there is only death.'

sentences.zh: 」好問曰：「死不難，誠能安社稷、救生靈，死而可也。

translations.literal: Haowen said: 'Death is not difficult; if one can truly settle the altars of soil and grain and save the living, then death is acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: Haowen said, 'Death is easy enough—but if it would truly save the state and the people, then death is fitting.'

sentences.zh: 如其不然，徒欲一身飽五十紅衲軍，亦謂之死耶？

translations.literal: If it is not so, merely wishing to fill one's own belly and those of fifty red-robed troops—is that also called death?'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, is it death merely to fill your own bellies and those of your fifty red-robed guards?'

sentences.zh: 」阿不款語曰：「今日惟吾二人，何言不可。

translations.literal: A-bu spoke earnestly: 'Today there are only we two—what may we not say?'
translations.idiomatic: A-bu spoke frankly: 'Today it is only the two of us—what cannot be said?'

sentences.zh: 」好問乃曰：「聞中外人言，欲立二王監國，以全兩宮與皇族耳。

translations.literal: Haowen then said: 'I hear people inside and outside say they wish to establish the two princes as regents to preserve the two palaces and the imperial clan.'
translations.idiomatic: Haowen then said, 'I hear talk everywhere of installing the two princes as regents to preserve the empresses and the imperial clan.'

sentences.zh: 」阿不曰：「我知之矣，我知之矣。

translations.literal: A-bu said: 'I know it, I know it.'
translations.idiomatic: A-bu said, 'I know, I know.'

sentences.zh: 」即命召京城官民。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the officials and people of the capital summoned.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered officials and citizens of the capital summoned.

sentences.zh: 明日皆聚省中，諭以事勢危急當如之何。

translations.literal: The next day all gathered in the Secretariat; they were instructed on how to act given that affairs were critically urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they all assembled at the Secretariat and were asked what should be done in the present extremity.

sentences.zh: 有父老七人陳詞云云，二相命好問受其詞。

translations.literal: Seven elders among the people presented their statements; the two chancellors ordered Haowen to receive their words.
translations.idiomatic: Seven elders among the people spoke at length; the two chancellors had Haowen record their statements.

sentences.zh: 白之奴申，顧曰：「亦為此事也。

translations.literal: Reporting to Nushen, he looked back and said: 'It is also for this matter.'
translations.idiomatic: When he reported to Nushen, Nushen turned and said, 'So it is for this as well.'

sentences.zh: 」且問副樞「此事謀議今幾日矣」？

translations.literal: And he asked the Vice Commissioner, 'For how many days has this matter been deliberated?'
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the Vice Commissioner, 'How long has this been under discussion?'

sentences.zh: 阿不屈指曰：「七日矣。

translations.literal: A-bu bent his finger and said: 'Seven days.'
translations.idiomatic: A-bu counted on his fingers and said, 'Seven days.'

sentences.zh: 」奴申曰：」歸德使未去，慎勿泄。

translations.literal: Nushen said: 'The envoy from Guide has not yet departed—take care not to leak this.'
translations.idiomatic: Nushen said, 'The envoy from Guide has not yet left—be careful not to let this out.'

sentences.zh: 」或曰是時週邊不解，如在陷阱，議者欲推立荊王以城出降，是亦《春秋》紀季入齊之義，況北兵中已有曹王也。

translations.literal: Some say that at this time the surroundings were not relieved, as if in a trap; those deliberating wished to advance Prince Jing and surrender the city with him—this was also the meaning of Jiji's entering Qi in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and moreover Prince Cao was already among the northern troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the city was surrounded with no escape, as in a trap; advocates wished to install Prince Jing and surrender the city—the logic of Jiji yielding Qi in the Spring and Autumn Annals—and Prince Cao was already a hostage in the Mongol camp.

sentences.zh: 眾憤二人無策，但曰死守而已。

translations.literal: The crowd was angry that the two men had no plan and only said to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was furious that the two ministers had no plan and could only urge holding the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 忽聞召京城士庶計事，奴申拱立無語，獨阿不反復申諭：「國家至此無可奈何，凡有可行當共議之」，且繼以涕泣。

translations.literal: Suddenly hearing that the gentry and commoners of the capital had been summoned to deliberate, Nushen stood with folded hands and said nothing; only A-bu repeatedly instructed: 'The state has come to this pass with nothing to be done; whatever can be done should be discussed together,' and followed with weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital's elite and commoners were suddenly summoned to counsel, Nushen stood silent with folded hands. Only A-bu pleaded again and again, 'The state is helpless; let us discuss whatever may yet be done,' and wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 明日戊辰，西面元帥崔立與其党孛術魯長哥、韓鐸、藥安國等為變，率甲卒二百橫刀入省中，拔劍指二相曰：「京城危困已極，二公坐視百姓餓死，恬不為慮，何也？

translations.literal: On the next day, wuchen, the western marshal Cui Li with his faction Boshulu Changge, Han Duo, Yao Anguo, and others made a mutiny, leading two hundred armored soldiers with swords bared into the Secretariat, drawing swords and pointing at the two chancellors: 'The capital's peril and distress have reached the extreme; you two sit and watch the people starve to death and are calmly unconcerned—why?'
translations.idiomatic: The next day, on wuchen, western marshal Cui Li and his followers Boshulu Changge, Han Duo, Yao Anguo, and others mutinied. Two hundred armed men burst into the Secretariat with blades drawn. Cui Li pointed his sword at the two chancellors and demanded, 'The capital is at its last extremity. You sit by while the people starve and show no concern—why?'

sentences.zh: 」二相大駭，曰：「汝輩有事，當好議之，何遽如是。

translations.literal: The two chancellors were greatly alarmed and said: 'If you fellows have business, it should be well discussed—why so suddenly like this?'
translations.idiomatic: The two chancellors were terrified. 'If you have grievances,' they said, 'let us discuss them properly—why act so rashly?'

sentences.zh: 」立麾其党先殺阿不，次殺奴申及左司郎中納合德輝等，余見《崔立傳》。

translations.literal: Li waved his faction to kill A-bu first, then kill Nushen and Left Bureau Director Nahan Dehui and others; the rest is in the Biography of Cui Li.
translations.idiomatic: Li ordered his men to kill A-bu first, then Nushen and Left Bureau Director Nahan Dehui and others; the rest is told in the Biography of Cui Li.

sentences.zh: 劉祁曰：「金自南渡之後，為宰執者往往無恢復之謀，臨事相習低言緩語，互相推讓，以為養相體。

translations.literal: Liu Qi said: 'Since the Jin moved south of the river, those who served as chief ministers often had no plans for restoration; when facing affairs they were accustomed to low voices and slow speech, pushing responsibility on one another, thinking this cultivated the ministerial demeanor.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi wrote: 'After the Jin moved south, their chief ministers seldom planned for recovery. In crisis they spoke softly and slowly, deferring to one another, calling this the proper bearing of a statesman.'

sentences.zh: 每有四方災異、民間疾苦，將奏必相謂曰：'恐聖主心困。

translations.literal: Whenever there were calamities in the four directions or suffering among the people, before memorializing they would say to one another: 'We fear troubling the sage ruler's mind.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever disasters struck the realm or the people suffered, before memorializing they would tell one another, 'We must not weary the emperor's heart.'

sentences.zh: '事至危處輒罷散，曰'俟再議'，已而複然。

translations.literal: When affairs reached a critical point they would adjourn, saying 'wait to discuss again,' and afterward it would be the same again.
translations.idiomatic: When matters grew desperate they adjourned, saying 'let us discuss again later'—and later it was always the same.

sentences.zh: 或有言當改革者，輒以生事抑之，故所用必擇軟熟無鋒芒易制者用之。

translations.literal: If anyone spoke of needing reform, they would suppress it as stirring up trouble; therefore those employed were invariably chosen for being soft, smooth, without edge, and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who urged reform was silenced as a troublemaker. They chose only men who were pliant, bland, and easy to manage.

sentences.zh: 每北兵壓境，則君臣相對泣下，或殿上發長籲而已。

translations.literal: Whenever northern troops pressed the borders, ruler and ministers would face one another weeping, or on the hall issue long sighs and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever northern armies pressed the frontier, emperor and ministers wept together—or sighed long on the throne and did nothing more.

sentences.zh: 兵退，則大張具，會飲黃閣中矣。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew, they would spread a great feast and meet to drink in the Yellow Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, they spread lavish banquets and feasted in the Yellow Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 因循苟且，竟至亡國。

translations.literal: Dragging on in compromise and expediency, they finally reached the loss of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Through delay and expediency they brought the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 又多取渾厚少文者置之台鼎，宣宗嘗責丞相僕散七斤'近來朝廷紀綱安在'？

translations.literal: They also took many who were honest and thick and placed them at the pinnacle of state; Emperor Xuanzong once reproached Grand Councillor Pushe Qijin: 'Where lately is the discipline of the court?'
translations.idiomatic: They favored dull, unlettered men for the highest posts. Emperor Xuanzong once rebuked Grand Councillor Pushe Qijin: 'Where has the discipline of this court gone?'

sentences.zh: 七斤不能對，退謂郎官曰：'上問紀綱安在，汝等自來何嘗使紀綱見我。

translations.literal: Qijin could not answer; retiring he said to the bureau officials: 'The emperor asks where discipline is—when have you ever let discipline appear before me?'
translations.idiomatic: Qijin had no reply. Retiring, he told his staff, 'The emperor asks where discipline has gone—when have you ever let me exercise any?'

sentences.zh: '故正人君子多不見用，雖用亦未久而遽退也。

translations.literal: Therefore upright gentlemen were mostly not employed; even if employed, it was not long before they were hastily removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus upright men were seldom employed, and even when used were soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」祁字京叔，渾源人。

translations.literal: Qi, courtesy name Jingshu, was a man of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, whose courtesy name was Jingshu, was from Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：劉京叔《歸潛志》與元裕之《壬辰雜編》二書雖微有異同，而金末喪亂之事猶有足征者焉。

translations.literal: The comment says: Liu Jingshu's Returning to Seclusion and Yuan Yuzhi's Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen Year, though they differ slightly, still offer sufficient testimony concerning the disorders at the end of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator notes: Liu Jingshu's Returning to Seclusion and Yuan Haowen's Miscellaneous Records of the Renchen Year differ in small ways, yet both preserve valuable testimony to the Jin dynasty's final collapse.

sentences.zh: 哀宗北禦，以孤城弱卒托之奴申、阿不二人，可謂難矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong went north to resist, entrusting a lone city and weak troops to Nushen and A-bu, the two—it may be said—had a difficult charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong marched north, he left a besieged city and feeble garrison to Nushen and A-bu—a burden few could bear.

sentences.zh: 雖然，即墨有安平君，玉壁有韋孝寬，必有以處此。

translations.literal: Even so, at Jimo there was Lord Pingyuan, at Yubi there was Wei Xiaokuan—there must be a way to deal with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jimo had Lord Pingyuan and Yubi had Wei Xiaokuan—surely there were men who could have met such a crisis.

sentences.zh: 藥安國者，管州人，年二十餘，有勇力。

translations.literal: Yao Anguo was a man of Guanzhou, over twenty years of age, with courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Anguo was from Guanzhou, in his twenties, brave and strong.

sentences.zh: 嘗為嵐州招撫使，以罪系開封獄，既出，貧無以為食。

translations.literal: He had once been Pacification Commissioner of Lanzhou; for a crime he was imprisoned in Kaifeng jail; after release he was poor with nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as Pacification Commissioner of Lanzhou, was imprisoned in Kaifeng for a crime, and after release was destitute and starving.

sentences.zh: 立將為變，潛結納之，安國健啖，日飽之以魚，遂與之謀。

translations.literal: As Li was about to mutiny, he secretly won him over; Anguo ate heartily; daily he fed him his fill with fish, and then plotted with him.
translations.idiomatic: As Cui Li prepared his coup, he secretly recruited Anguo, who had a hearty appetite; Li fed him fish daily until they plotted together.

sentences.zh: 先以家置西城上，事不勝則挈以逃。

translations.literal: First he placed his family on the western wall; if the affair did not succeed he would take them and flee.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed his family on the western wall beforehand so that if the plot failed he could flee with them.

sentences.zh: 日與都尉楊善入省中候動靜，佈置已定，召善以早食，殺之。

translations.literal: Daily he and Commandant Yang Shan entered the Secretariat to watch developments; when arrangements were set, he summoned Shan for an early meal and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he and Commandant Yang Shan entered the Secretariat to watch for developments. When all was ready, he summoned Yang for breakfast and killed him.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，遂帥甲卒二百，撞省門而入。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he then led two hundred armored soldiers, rammed the Secretariat gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he led two hundred soldiers, smashed through the Secretariat gate, and burst in.

sentences.zh: 二相聞變趨出，立拔劍曰：「京城危困，二公欲如何處之？

translations.literal: The two chancellors, hearing of the mutiny, hurried out; Li drew his sword and said: 'The capital is in peril and distress—how do you two intend to deal with it?'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, the two chancellors rushed out. Li drew his sword and demanded, 'The capital is desperate—what do you two intend to do?'

sentences.zh: 」二相曰：「事當好議之。

translations.literal: The two chancellors said: 'The matter should be well discussed.'
translations.idiomatic: The two chancellors said, 'Let us discuss this properly.'

sentences.zh: 」立不顧，麾其党張信之、孛術魯長哥出省，二相遂遇害。

translations.literal: Li paid no heed, waved his faction Zhang Xinzhi and Boshulu Changge out of the Secretariat, and the two chancellors were thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li ignored them, sent his followers Zhang Xinzhi and Boshulu Changge from the hall, and the two chancellors were slain.

sentences.zh: 馳往東華門，道遇點檢溫屯阿裏，見其衷甲，殺之。

translations.literal: He galloped to the Eastern Flowery Gate; on the road he met Inspector Wentun Ali, saw that he wore armor beneath his robe, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to the Eastern Flowery Gate, met Inspector Wentun Ali on the way, saw armor under his robe, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 即諭百姓曰：「吾為二相閉門無謀，今殺之，為汝一城生靈請命。

translations.literal: He immediately instructed the people: 'I killed the two chancellors because they shut the gates with no plan—now I have killed them to plead for the lives of all of you in this city.'
translations.idiomatic: He announced to the people, 'The two chancellors shut the gates and had no plan. I have killed them to plead for the lives of everyone in this city.'

sentences.zh: 」眾皆稱快。

translations.literal: The crowd all expressed satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd cheered.

sentences.zh: 是日，御史大夫裴滿阿忽帶、諫議大夫左右司郎中烏古孫奴申、左副點檢完顏阿散、奉禦忙哥、講議蒲察琦、戶部尚書完顏珠顆皆死。

translations.literal: That day Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai, Remonstrating Censor and Left and Right Bureau Director Wugusun Nushen, Left Deputy Inspector Wanyan Asan, Attendant-in-Waiting Mangge, Deliberator Pucha Qi, and Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke all died.
translations.idiomatic: That day Censor-in-Chief Peiman Ahudai, Remonstrating Censor and Bureau Director Wugusun Nushen, Deputy Inspector Wanyan Asan, Attendant-in-Waiting Mangge, Deliberator Pucha Qi, and Minister of Revenue Wanyan Zhuke were all killed.

sentences.zh: 立還省中，集百官議所立。

translations.literal: Li returned to the Secretariat, gathered all officials, and deliberated whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: Li returned to the Secretariat and assembled the officials to decide whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 立曰：「衛紹王太子從恪，其妹公主在北兵中，可立之。

translations.literal: Li said: 'Prince Congke, son of Prince Shao of Wei—his sister the princess is among the northern troops; he may be established.'
translations.idiomatic: Li said, 'Prince Congke, heir of Prince Shao of Wei, has a sister the princess already among the Mongols—he should be enthroned.'

sentences.zh: 」乃遣其党韓鐸以太后命往召從恪。

translations.literal: He then sent his follower Han Duo with the empress dowager's command to summon Congke.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his follower Han Duo with the empress dowager's order to fetch Congke.

sentences.zh: 須臾入，以太后誥命梁王監國。

translations.literal: In a moment he entered; by the empress dowager's patent edict Prince Liang was made regent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he arrived, and by the empress dowager's edict Prince Liang was named regent.

sentences.zh: 百官拜舞山呼，從恪受之，遂遣送二相所佩虎符詣速不泬納款。

translations.literal: All officials bowed, danced, and shouted like a mountain; Congke received it; then he sent the tiger tallies worn by the two chancellors to Subutai to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bowed and shouted their acclamation; Congke accepted the regency and sent the two chancellors' tiger tallies to Subutai to surrender.

sentences.zh: 凡除拜皆以監國為辭。

translations.literal: All appointments and dismissals were made in the name of the regent.
translations.idiomatic: Every appointment was issued in the regent's name.

sentences.zh: 立自稱太師、軍馬都元帥、尚書令、鄭王，出入禦乘輿，稱其妻為王妃，弟倚為平章政事，侃為殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: Li styled himself Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of Armies and Horses, Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Zheng; he went in and out riding the imperial carriage, called his wife princess consort, his younger brother Yi Grand Councillor, and Kan Chief Inspector of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: Li styled himself Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Zheng; he rode the imperial carriage, called his wife princess consort, made his brother Yi Grand Councillor and Kan Chief Palace Inspector.

sentences.zh: 其党孛術魯長哥御史中丞，韓鐸都元帥兼知開封府事，折希顏、藥安國、張軍奴並元帥，師肅左右司郎中，賈良兵部郎中兼右司都事，內府之事皆主之。

translations.literal: His faction: Boshulu Changge Censor-in-Chief; Han Duo Commander-in-Chief and concurrent Administrator of Kaifeng; Zhe Xiyan, Yao Anguo, and Zhang Junnu all marshals; Shi Su Left and Right Bureau Director; Jia Liang Bureau Director of War and concurrent Right Bureau Director—all inner-palace affairs were directed by them.
translations.idiomatic: His followers received high posts: Boshulu Changge as Censor-in-Chief; Han Duo as Commander-in-Chief and Administrator of Kaifeng; Zhe Xiyan, Yao Anguo, and Zhang Junnu as marshals; Shi Su and Jia Liang in the Secretariat—they controlled all palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，立假安國之勇以濟事，至是複忌之，聞安國納一都尉夫人，數其違約斬之。

translations.literal: At first Li borrowed Anguo's courage to accomplish the affair; by this time he again envied him; hearing that Anguo had taken a commandant's wife, he counted his breach of agreement and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li had relied on Anguo's bravery; now he grew jealous. Learning Anguo had taken a commandant's wife, he accused him of breaking their pact and executed him.

sentences.zh: 壬申，速不泬至青城，立服禦衣，儀衛往見之。

translations.literal: On renshen day Subutai reached Qingcheng; Li wore imperial robes and went with ceremonial guards to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Subutai reached Qingcheng. Li donned imperial robes and went out with full escort to meet him.

sentences.zh: 大帥喜，飲之酒，立以父事之。

translations.literal: The supreme commander was pleased, gave him wine to drink, and Li treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander was pleased, offered him wine, and Li treated him with filial deference.

sentences.zh: 既還，悉燒京城樓櫓，火起，大帥大喜，始信其實降也。

translations.literal: After returning, he burned all the towers and stockades of the capital; when the fires rose, the supreme commander was greatly pleased and for the first time believed the surrender was real.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he burned all the capital's towers and ramparts. When the flames rose, the supreme commander rejoiced and at last believed the surrender genuine.

sentences.zh: 立托以軍前索隨駕官吏家屬，聚之省中，人自閱之，日亂數人猶若不足。

translations.literal: Li pretended that the army front demanded the families of officials who had followed the imperial progress; he gathered them in the Secretariat for people to choose for themselves; daily he molested several persons and still seemed not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Li claimed the Mongol camp demanded the families of officials who had accompanied the emperor. He herded them into the Secretariat for his men to pick at will, violating several people a day and still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 又禁城中嫁娶，有以一女之故殺數人者。

translations.literal: He also forbade marriage within the city; for the sake of one girl several people were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade weddings in the city; over a single girl several men were killed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷梁王及宗室近族皆置宮中，以腹心守之，限其出入。

translations.literal: Before long he moved Prince Liang and the close kin of the imperial clan all into the palace, guarded them with trusted men, and restricted their coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he confined Prince Liang and the nearest imperial kin inside the palace under trusted guards, restricting their movements.

sentences.zh: 以荊王府為私第，取內府珍玩實之。

translations.literal: He took Prince Jing's mansion as his private residence and filled it with precious curios from the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Prince Jing's mansion for his private residence and stocked it with treasures from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 二月乙酉，以天子袞冕後服上進。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the second month he presented the emperor's ceremonial robes and rear garments as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the second month he presented the emperor's state robes and regalia to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 又括在城金銀，搜索薰灌，訊掠慘酷，百苦備至。

translations.literal: He also seized gold and silver within the city, searched with fumigation and pouring, interrogated and plundered with cruel severity—all hundred sufferings were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He confiscated all gold and silver in the city, searched homes by smoke and flood, tortured victims in interrogation—every cruelty imaginable was inflicted.

sentences.zh: 郕國夫人及內侍高佑、京民李民望之屬，皆死杖下。

translations.literal: Lady of the State of Xing, the inner attendant Gao You, the capital resident Li Minwang, and their kind all died under the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Xing, the eunuch Gao You, the citizen Li Minwang, and others all died under beating.

sentences.zh: 溫屯衛尉親屬八人，不任楚毒，皆自盡。

translations.literal: Eight relatives of the Commandant of the Guards Wentun, unable to bear the Chu torture, all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Eight relatives of Commandant Wentun, unable to endure torture, all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 白撒夫人、右丞李蹊妻子皆被掠死。

translations.literal: Lady Baisa, the wife and children of Right Vice Councillor Li Xi—all were seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Baisa and the wife and children of Right Vice Councillor Li Xi were seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 同惡相濟，視人如仇，期於必報而後已。

translations.literal: Evil men aided one another, regarded people as enemies, and would not stop until they had surely revenged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They aided one another in wickedness, treated everyone as an enemy, and would not rest until every score was settled.

sentences.zh: 人人竊相謂曰：「攻城之後七八日之中，諸門出葬者開封府計之凡百余萬人，恨不早預其數而值此不幸也。

translations.literal: Everyone whispered to one another: 'In the seven or eight days after the siege, those going out for burial at the various gates—the Kaifeng prefecture counted them at more than a million; they regretted not having joined that number earlier and instead meeting this misfortune.'
translations.idiomatic: People whispered among themselves, 'In the week after the siege, Kaifeng prefecture counted more than a million corpses carried out for burial. We regret not having died then rather than suffer this.'

sentences.zh: 」立時與其妻入宮，兩宮賜之不可勝計。

translations.literal: Li at times entered the palace with his wife; the two palaces bestowed on them beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li and his wife often entered the palace, and the empresses showered them with gifts beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 立因諷太后作書陳天時人事，遣皇乳母招歸德。

translations.literal: Li therefore prompted the empress dowager to write a letter setting forth heaven's seasons and human affairs, and sent the imperial wet nurse to summon Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Li induced the empress dowager to write describing the cosmic and political situation, and sent the imperial wet nurse to summon the court at Guide.

sentences.zh: 當時冒進之徒爭援劉齊故事以冀非分者，比肩接武。

translations.literal: At that time the rashly ambitious vied to cite the precedents of Liu Yu and Qi, hoping for undue favor—shoulder to shoulder, rank upon rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious men crowded forward, each citing the puppet rulers Liu Yu and Qi in hope of unmerited power.

sentences.zh: 四月壬辰，立以兩宮、梁王、荊王及諸宗室皆赴青城，甲午北行，立妻王氏備仗衛送兩宮至開陽門。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the fourth month Li sent the two palaces, Prince Liang, Prince Jing, and all the imperial clan to Qingcheng; on the jiawu day they went north; Li's wife Lady Wang, with full ceremonial guards, escorted the two palaces to the Kaiyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the fourth month Li sent the empresses, Prince Liang, Prince Jing, and the entire imperial clan to Qingcheng. On jiawu day they departed north. Li's wife Lady Wang escorted the empresses to Kaiyang Gate with full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 是日，宮車三十七兩，太后先，中宮次之，妃嬪又次之，宗族男女凡五百餘口，次取三教、醫流、工匠、繡女皆赴北。

translations.literal: That day there were thirty-seven palace carriages—the empress dowager first, the central palace next, consorts and concubines after; clansmen and women totaled more than five hundred; next were taken clergy of the three teachings, physicians, craftsmen, and embroiderers—all went north.
translations.idiomatic: That day thirty-seven palace carriages set out—the empress dowager first, then the empress, then consorts. More than five hundred kinsmen followed, along with clergy, physicians, artisans, and embroiderers—all marched north.

sentences.zh: 四月，北兵入城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the northern troops entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the northern army entered the city.

sentences.zh: 立時在城外，兵先入其家，取其妻妾寶玉以出，立歸大慟，無如之何。

translations.literal: Li was then outside the city; troops first entered his house, took his wives, concubines, and jewels and came out; Li returned and wailed greatly, with nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Li was outside the walls when soldiers raided his house, seized his wives, concubines, and jewels. He returned home and wept bitterly, helpless.

sentences.zh: 李琦者，山西人，為都尉，在陳州與粘哥奴申同行省事，陳州變，入京，附崔立妹婿折希顏，娶夾谷元之妻，妻年二十余，有姿色，立初拘隨駕官之家屬，妻輿病而往，得免。

translations.literal: Li Qi was a man of Shanxi, a commandant; at Chenzhou he served with Niage Nushen as Branch Secretariat affairs officer; when Chenzhou mutinied he entered the capital, attached himself to Cui Li's brother-in-law Zhe Xiyan, and married the wife of Jiagu Yuan—she was over twenty, with beauty; when Li first detained the families of officials who had followed the imperial progress, the wife went in a litter feigning illness and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi of Shanxi had been a commandant at Chenzhou alongside Niage Nushen. After Chenzhou fell he fled to the capital and joined Cui Li's brother-in-law Zhe Xiyan. He married the young, beautiful widow of Jiagu Yuan. When Cui Li rounded up officials' families, she feigned illness in a litter and escaped detention.

sentences.zh: 琦娶之後，有言其美者，立欲強之。

translations.literal: After Qi married her, there were those who spoke of her beauty; Li wished to take her by force.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi married her, word of her beauty reached Cui Li, who sought to take her by force.

sentences.zh: 琦每見立欲奪人妻，必差其夫遠出，一日差琦出京，琦以妻自隨，如是者再三，立遂欲殺琦。

translations.literal: Whenever Qi saw Li wish to seize another man's wife, he would surely send the husband far away; one day he sent Qi out of the capital; Qi took his wife with him—thus several times; Li then wished to kill Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cui Li coveted another man's wife, he sent the husband away on distant duty. He dispatched Qi from the capital, but Qi took his wife along—three times in all. Cui Li then resolved to kill him.

sentences.zh: 琦又數為折希顏所折辱，乃首建殺立之謀。

translations.literal: Qi was also repeatedly humiliated by Zhe Xiyan; he then first proposed the plot to kill Li.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had also been repeatedly humiliated by Zhe Xiyan and was the first to propose killing Cui Li.

sentences.zh: 李伯淵者，寶坻人，本安平都尉司千戶，美姿容，深沉有謀，每憤立不道，欲仗義殺之。

translations.literal: Li Boyuan was a man of Baodi, originally a chiliarch of the Anping Commandant's office, with handsome features, deep and resourceful; he constantly resented Li's unrighteous conduct and wished to kill him in the name of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Boyuan of Baodi had been a chiliarch in the Anping commandery. Handsome and deep-thinking, he constantly raged at Cui Li's crimes and wished to slay him for righteousness' sake.

sentences.zh: 李賤奴者，燕人，嘗以軍功遙領京兆府判，壬辰冬，車駕東狩，以都尉權東面元帥。

translations.literal: Li Jiannu was a man of Yan; he had once by military merit held the distant post of Administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture; in the winter of the renchen year, when the imperial carriage went east on campaign, he was made commandant acting eastern marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiannu of Yan had earned a distant appointment as Administrator of Jingzhao through military service. In the winter of renchen year, when the emperor marched east, he was made acting eastern marshal.

sentences.zh: 立初反，以賤奴舊與敵體，頗貌敬之。

translations.literal: When Li first rebelled, because Jiannu had formerly been of equal standing with the enemy, he showed him considerable outward respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li first rebelled, he showed Jiannu outward respect because Jiannu had once been the emperor's equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 數月之後，勢已固，遂視賤奴如部曲然。

translations.literal: After several months his power was firm, and he then regarded Jiannu as a mere subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: After a few months, secure in power, he treated Jiannu like any other subordinate.

sentences.zh: 賤奴積不能平，數出怨言，至是與琦等合。

translations.literal: Jiannu's resentment accumulated without relief; he often uttered complaints; by this time he joined with Qi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannu's resentment festered; he voiced complaints repeatedly and now joined Qi and the others.

sentences.zh: 三年六月甲午，傳近境有宋軍，伯淵等陽與立謀備禦之策。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the sixth month of the third year, it was reported that Song troops were near the borders; Boyuan and the others pretended to discuss with Li plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the sixth month of the third year, word spread that Song armies were near. Boyuan and his allies feigned consultation with Cui Li on defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 翌日晚，伯淵等燒外封丘門以警動立。

translations.literal: The next evening Boyuan and the others burned the outer Fengqiu Gate to alarm and stir Li.
translations.idiomatic: That evening they set fire to the outer Fengqiu Gate to alarm Cui Li.

sentences.zh: 是夜，立殊不安，一夕百臥起。

translations.literal: That night Li was especially uneasy—within one night he rose from bed a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: That night Cui Li was deeply unsettled, rising from bed a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 比明，伯淵等身來約立視火，立從苑秀、折希顏數騎往，諭京城民十五以上、七十以下男子皆詣太廟街點集。

translations.literal: By dawn Boyuan and the others came in person to invite Li to view the fire; Li followed with Yuan Xiu, Zhe Xiyan, and several horsemen; he instructed that all men of the capital aged fifteen and above and seventy and below should assemble for roll call on Temple Street.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Boyuan came in person to invite Cui Li to inspect the fire. Cui Li rode out with Yuan Xiu, Zhe Xiyan, and a few horsemen, and ordered all men in the capital between fifteen and seventy to assemble on Temple Street.

sentences.zh: 既還，行及梳行街，伯淵欲送立還二王府，立辭數四，伯淵必欲親送，立不疑，倉卒中就馬上抱立。

translations.literal: After returning, as they reached Shuxing Street, Boyuan wished to escort Li back to the Second Prince's mansion; Li declined several times; Boyuan insisted on escorting him personally; Li suspected nothing; in haste he embraced Li on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: On the return, reaching Shuxing Street, Boyuan offered to escort Cui Li to the Second Prince's mansion. Cui Li declined repeatedly, but Boyuan insisted. Unsuspecting, Cui Li was seized on horseback in an instant.

sentences.zh: 立顧曰：「汝欲殺我耶？

translations.literal: Li looked back and said: 'Do you wish to kill me?'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li turned and cried, 'Do you mean to kill me?'

sentences.zh: 」伯淵曰：「殺汝何傷。

translations.literal: Boyuan said: 'What harm in killing you?'
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan said, 'What harm is there in killing you?'

sentences.zh: 」即出匕首橫刺之，洞而中其手之抱立處，再刺之，立墜馬死。

translations.literal: He then drew a dagger and stabbed horizontally; it pierced through to where his hand embraced Li; he stabbed again; Li fell from the horse dead.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his dagger and stabbed; the blade passed through his arm into Cui Li's body. He stabbed again, and Cui Li fell dead from his horse.

sentences.zh: 伏兵起，元帥黃摑三合殺苑秀。

translations.literal: Ambush troops rose; Marshal Huangpusa He killed Yuan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden troops sprang up; Marshal Huangpusa He killed Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 折希顏後至不知，見立墜馬，謂與人鬥，欲前解之，隨為軍士所斫，被創走梁門外，追斬之。

translations.literal: Zhe Xiyan arrived later unaware; seeing Li fall from his horse, he thought it a fight with someone and wished to go forward to separate them; he was immediately hacked by soldiers, wounded, fled outside the Liang Gate, and was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Xiyan arrived late and, seeing Cui Li fall, thought it a brawl and rushed to intervene. Soldiers cut him down; wounded, he fled beyond the Liang Gate and was pursued and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 伯淵系立屍馬尾，至內前號於眾曰：「立殺害劫奪，烝淫暴虐，大逆不道，古今無有，當殺之不？

translations.literal: Boyuan tied Li's corpse to a horse's tail, came before the inner palace, and shouted to the crowd: 'Li murdered, robbed, committed incest, was violent and cruel, utterly rebellious—unprecedented in past and present—should he not have been killed?'
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan dragged Cui Li's corpse by a horse's tail to the inner palace and cried to the crowd, 'Cui Li murdered, plundered, committed incest, and tyrannized beyond anything in history—was he not rightly killed?'

sentences.zh: 」萬口齊應曰：「寸斬之未稱也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand mouths answered together: 'Death by inch-long cuts would not be adequate.'
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand voices answered, 'Death by inches would be too merciful.'

sentences.zh: 」乃梟立首，望承天門祭哀宗。

translations.literal: They then displayed Li's head on a pole, facing the Gate of Receiving Heaven to offer sacrifice to Emperor Aizong.
translations.idiomatic: They displayed Cui Li's head on a pole facing the Gate of Receiving Heaven as an offering to Emperor Aizong.

sentences.zh: 伯淵以下軍民皆慟，或剖其心生啖之。

translations.literal: Boyuan and all below, soldiers and civilians, were moved to grief; some cut out his heart and began to eat it raw.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan and the soldiers and civilians wept; some cut out his heart and ate it raw.

sentences.zh: 以三屍掛闕前槐樹上，樹忽拔，人謂樹有靈，亦厭其為所汙。

translations.literal: The three corpses were hung on the locust tree before the palace gate; the tree suddenly uprooted itself; people said the tree had a spirit and also loathed being defiled by them.
translations.idiomatic: The three corpses were hung on the locust tree before the palace gate; the tree suddenly uprooted itself. People said the tree had a spirit and revolted at being defiled.

sentences.zh: 已而有告立匿宮中珍玩，遂籍其家，以其妻王花兒賜丞相鎮海帳下士。

translations.literal: Soon someone reported that Li had hidden palace treasures; his household was then registered and confiscated; his wife Wang Hua'er was bestowed on a soldier under Grand Councillor Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone reported hidden palace treasures; his property was confiscated and his wife Wang Hua'er given to a soldier under Grand Councillor Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 初，立之變也，前護衛蒲鮮石魯負祖宗禦容五，走蔡。

translations.literal: At the time of Li's mutiny, former guard Puxian Shilu carried off five imperial portraits of the ancestors and fled to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Li mutinied, former guard Puxian Shilu carried off five imperial ancestral portraits and fled to Cai.

sentences.zh: 前御史中丞蒲察世達、西面元帥把撒合挈其家亦自拔歸蔡。

translations.literal: Former Censor-in-Chief Pucha Shida and western marshal Basage, taking their families, also broke through and returned to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Former Censor-in-Chief Pucha Shida and western marshal Basage also broke through with their families and fled to Cai.

sentences.zh: 七月己巳，以世達為尚書吏部侍郎，權行六部尚書。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the seventh month Shida was made Vice Minister of Personnel of the Secretariat and Acting Director of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the seventh month Shida was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Acting Director of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 世達嘗為左司郎中，同簽樞密院事，充益政院官，皆稱上意。

translations.literal: Shida had once been Left Bureau Director, Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and officer of the Beneficial Governance Academy—all were praised as meeting the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shida had served as Left Bureau Director, Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and officer of the Beneficial Governance Academy—all roles in which he pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及上幸歸德，遣世達督陳糧運。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Guide, he sent Shida to supervise Chen grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Guide, he sent Shida to oversee grain shipments from Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳變，世達亦與脅從，尋間道之汴，至是徒往行在，上念其舊，錄用之。

translations.literal: When Chen mutinied, Shida was also compelled to follow; soon he took a bypath to Bian; by this time he had gone in vain to the mobile court; the emperor, remembering his past service, employed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen rebelled, Shida was forced along; he later found a secret route to Bian and then made his way to the mobile court. The emperor, remembering his past service, took him back into office.

sentences.zh: 左右司官因奏把撒合、石魯亦宜任用，上曰：「世達曲從，非出得已，然朕猶少降資級，以示薄罰。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Bureau officials thereupon memorialized that Basage and Shilu also ought to be employed; the emperor said: 'Shida bent to follow—not of his own will—yet I still slightly lowered his rank to show a light punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat officials urged that Basage and Shilu also be employed. The emperor said, 'Shida submitted under duress, not willingly—yet I still lowered his rank slightly as a light punishment.'

sentences.zh: 彼撒合掌軍一面，石魯宿衛九重，崔立之變，曾不聞發一矢，束手於人。

translations.literal: Those two—Basage commanded one army wing, Shilu guarded the ninefold palace—at Cui Li's mutiny, not a single arrow was heard loosed; they bound their hands and submitted to others.
translations.idiomatic: Basage commanded an army wing; Shilu guarded the palace. At Cui Li's mutiny neither loosed a single arrow—they submitted helplessly.

sentences.zh: 今雖來歸，待以不死，足以示恩，又安得與世達等？

translations.literal: Now though they have come back, to spare their lives is enough to show favor—how can they be ranked with Shida and the like?'
translations.idiomatic: Though they have returned, sparing their lives is grace enough—how can they be treated like Shida?'

sentences.zh: 撒合老矣，量用其子可也。

translations.literal: Basage is old; it is enough to employ his son as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Basage is old; employing his son will suffice.

sentences.zh: 石魯但當酬其負禦容之勞。

translations.literal: Shilu need only be rewarded for the labor of carrying off the imperial portraits.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu need only be rewarded for rescuing the imperial portraits.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，以撒合為北門都尉，其子為本軍都統。

translations.literal: Before long Basage was made Commandant of the North Gate and his son Commander of the native army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Basage was made Commandant of the North Gate and his son commander of the native army.

sentences.zh: 石魯複充護衛。

translations.literal: Shilu again served as guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu was restored to the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 世達字正夫，泰和三年進士。

translations.literal: Shida, courtesy name Zhengfu, was a jinshi of the third year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Shida, courtesy name Zhengfu, passed the jinshi examination in Taihe 3.

sentences.zh: 論曰：崔立納款，使其封府庫、籍人民以俟大朝之命可也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: For Cui Li to offer surrender, seal the treasuries, and register the people to await the Great Court's command—that would have been acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Had Cui Li simply surrendered, sealed the treasuries, registered the people, and awaited the Great Court's orders—that would have sufficed.

sentences.zh: 乘時僭竊，大肆淫虐，征索暴橫，輒以供備大軍為辭，逞欲由己，斂怨歸國，其為罪不容誅矣。

translations.literal: Seizing the moment to usurp power, he wildly indulged in lust and cruelty, levied and seized with violent arrogance, always using provision for the great army as pretext, gratifying his desires as he pleased, gathering resentment upon the state—his crimes could not be pardoned by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he seized power, indulged in lust and cruelty, extorted the people under pretense of provisioning the army, gratified his own desires, and heaped hatred on the state—crimes beyond any punishment.

sentences.zh: 而其志方且要求劉豫之事，我大朝豈肯效尤金人者乎！

translations.literal: Yet his ambition was even to demand the affair of Liu Yu—would our Great Court imitate the Jin in such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: His ambition even reached for the puppet throne of Liu Yu—would our Great Court imitate what the Jin had done!

sentences.zh: 金俘人之主，帝人之臣，百年之後適啟崔立之狂謀，以成青城之烈禍。

translations.literal: The Jin captured others' rulers and made them subjects of their emperor; a hundred years later this precisely opened Cui Li's mad plot and brought about the fierce calamity of Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had made captive emperors serve their own ruler; a century later that precedent inspired Cui Li's mad plot and the catastrophe at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 曾子曰：「戒之戒之，出乎爾者，反乎爾者也。

translations.literal: Master Zeng said: 'Be warned, be warned—what goes out from you returns upon you.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Zeng said, 'Take heed, take heed—what you do to others will return upon you.'

sentences.zh: 」豈不信哉！

translations.literal: Is it not believable!
translations.idiomatic: Can this not be believed!

sentences.zh: 聶天驥

translations.literal: Nie Tianji
translations.idiomatic: Nie Tianji

sentences.zh: 聶天驥，字元吉，五台人。

translations.literal: Nie Tianji, courtesy name Yuanji, was a man of Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Tianji, whose courtesy name was Yuanji, was from Wutai.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年進士，調汝陰簿，曆睢州司候、封丘令。

translations.literal: He was a jinshi in the first year of Zhibing, appointed registrar of Ruyin, and served successively as judicial officer of Suizhou and magistrate of Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhibing 1, served as registrar of Ruyin, and rose through posts as judicial officer of Suizhou and magistrate of Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 興定初，辟為尚書省令史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding he was recruited as clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xingding he was recruited as a Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 時胥吏擅威，士人往往附之，獨天驥不少假借，彼亦不能害也。

translations.literal: At that time clerks monopolized power; gentlemen often attached themselves to them—only Tianji would not yield to them in the least, and they could not harm him either.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks then wielded unchecked power and scholars often curried their favor. Tianji alone refused to yield, and they could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部主事，權監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bureau Director of Personnel and Acting Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Bureau Director of Personnel and Acting Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 夏使賀正旦，互市于會同館，外戚有身貿易於其間者，天驥上章曰：「大官近利，失朝廷體，且取輕外方。

translations.literal: When Xia envoys came to congratulate on New Year's Day, they traded at the Hall of Mutual Accord; among them a maternal relative personally traded; Tianji memorialized: 'Great officials near profit lose the court's dignity and moreover invite contempt from foreigners.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xia envoys came for New Year congratulations, trade was held at the Hall of Mutual Accord. A maternal relative of the court traded there in person. Tianji memorialized, 'When high officials pursue profit, the court loses dignity and foreign envoys hold us in contempt.'

sentences.zh: 」遂忤太后旨。

translations.literal: He thereby offended the empress dowager's intent.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 出為同知汝州防禦使事，未赴，陝西行尚書省驛召，特旨遙領金安軍節度副使，兼行尚書省都事。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Associate Administrator of the Defense Command of Ruzhou; before he took up the post, the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat summoned him by courier; by special edict he held the distant post of Vice Military Commissioner of Jin'an Army and concurrent Director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Associate Administrator of Ruzhou but before departing was summoned by the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. By special edict he was named Vice Military Commissioner of Jin'an and concurrent Director of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，人為右司員外郎，轉京兆治中，尋為衛州行尚書六部事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Right Bureau Vice Director, transferred to Administrator of Jingzhao, and soon made affairs officer of the Six Ministries of the Weizhou Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Bureau Vice Director, then Administrator of Jingzhao, and soon after affairs officer of the Six Ministries at the Weizhou branch.

sentences.zh: 慶陽圍急，朝廷遣宿州總帥牙古塔救之，以天驥充經歷官。

translations.literal: When the siege of Qingyang grew urgent, the court sent Suzhou Commander-in-Chief Yaguta to rescue it, with Tianji as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyang was besieged, the court sent Suzhou Commander-in-Chief Yaguta to the rescue, with Tianji as his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 圍解，從別帥守邠，帥欲棄州而東，天驥力勸止之，不從，帥坐是被系逮，天驥降京兆治中。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he followed another commander to hold Bin; the commander wished to abandon the prefecture and go east; Tianji strongly urged him to stop; he did not listen; the commander was therefore arrested and bound; Tianji was demoted to Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted he followed another commander to defend Bin. When the commander wished to abandon the prefecture and flee east, Tianji strongly dissuaded him in vain. The commander was arrested; Tianji was demoted to Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 尋有訟其冤者，即召為開封簽事，旬月複右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon someone sued on his behalf regarding the injustice; he was immediately summoned as Signing Officer of Kaifeng; within a month he was restored to Right Bureau Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a petition on his behalf reached the court; he was recalled as Signing Officer of Kaifeng and within a month restored to Right Bureau Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，未卒哭，奪哀複職。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; before the mourning rites were completed, he was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother but was recalled to office before the rites were finished.

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，天驥留汴中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong moved to Guide, Tianji remained in Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 崔立變，天驥被創甚，臥一十餘日。

translations.literal: At Cui Li's mutiny Tianji was badly wounded and lay abed more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: At Cui Li's mutiny Tianji was badly wounded and lay abed for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 其女舜英謁醫救療，天驥歎曰：「吾幸得死，兒女曹乃為謁醫，尚欲我活耶？

translations.literal: His daughter Shunying sought physicians to save him; Tianji sighed and said: 'I am fortunate to die—my children go begging doctors; do they still wish me to live?'
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Shunying sought physicians to heal him. Tianji sighed, 'I am fortunate to die—must my children beg doctors and wish me to live?'

sentences.zh: 」竟鬱鬱以死。

translations.literal: In the end he died in gloom.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 舜英葬其父，明日亦自縊，有傳。

translations.literal: Shunying buried her father; the next day she also hanged herself—there is a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shunying buried her father; the next day she hanged herself. A biography of her survives.

sentences.zh: 天驥沉靜寡言，不妄交。

translations.literal: Tianji was calm and reticent, not making friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Tianji was calm and sparing of speech, making friends only with care.

sentences.zh: 起於田畝，能以雅道自將，踐曆台省若素宦然，諸人多自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Rising from the fields, he could conduct himself by refined principle; passing through the terrace and secretariat as if a lifelong official—many considered themselves his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose from the fields, he conducted himself with refined principle and moved through high office as if born to it; many felt themselves his inferior.

sentences.zh: 赤盞尉忻

translations.literal: Chizhan Weixin
translations.idiomatic: Chizhan Weixin

sentences.zh: 赤盞尉忻，字大用，上京人。

translations.literal: Chizhan Weixin, courtesy name Dayong, was a man of Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhan Weixin, whose courtesy name was Dayong, was from Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 當襲其父謀克，不願就，中明昌五年策論進士第。

translations.literal: He was to inherit his father's office of mouke but did not wish to take it; he passed the Policy Essays jinshi in the fifth year of Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was to inherit his father's mouke office but declined it, passing the jinshi examination in Policy Essays in Mingchang 5.

sentences.zh: 後選為尚書省令史、吏部主事、監察御史，言「諸王駙馬至京師和買諸物，失朝廷體。

translations.literal: Later he was selected as Secretariat clerk, Bureau Director of Personnel, and Supervising Censor, stating: 'When princes and imperial sons-in-law come to the capital and forcibly purchase goods, the court loses dignity.'
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as Secretariat clerk, Bureau Director of Personnel, and Supervising Censor, memorializing that when princes and imperial sons-in-law came to the capital and forcibly purchased goods, the court lost dignity.

sentences.zh: 」有詔禁止。

translations.literal: An edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade the practice.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮南軍節度副使、息州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army and Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army and Prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 耕鞠場種禾，兩禾合穗，進於朝，特詔褒諭。

translations.literal: He plowed the cuju field and planted grain; two stalks joined in one ear; he presented it to the court and received a special edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He planted grain in the cuju field and produced two stalks joined in one ear, which he presented to the court and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 改丹州，遷鄭州防禦使，權許州統軍使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Danzhou, promoted to Defense Commissioner of Zhengzhou, and Acting Commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Danzhou, then made Defense Commissioner of Zhengzhou and Acting Commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丞相高汝礪嘗薦其才可任宰相。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Gao Ruli once recommended that his talent could fill the post of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Gao Ruli once recommended him as fit for the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 元光二年正月，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Yuanguang he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanguang 2 he was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，權參知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was Acting Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Acting Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 二月，為戶部尚書，權職如故。

translations.literal: In the second month he was made Minister of Revenue, his acting duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was made Minister of Revenue while retaining his acting councillor duties.

sentences.zh: 三月，拜參知政事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Compiler of the National History.

sentences.zh: 詔諭近臣曰：「尉忻資稟純質，事可倚任，且其性孝，朕今相之，國家必有望，汝輩當效之也。

translations.literal: An edict instructed the close ministers: 'Weixin's endowment is pure and simple; in affairs he may be relied upon, and moreover he is filial by nature. I now make him councillor—the state must have hope; you should take him as model.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict told the close ministers, 'Weixin is pure and trustworthy, and filial by nature. I appoint him councillor—the state may yet have hope. You should follow his example.'

sentences.zh: 」正大元年五月，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhengda he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhengda 1 he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哀宗欲修宮室，尉忻極諫，至是臥薪嚐膽為言，上悚然從之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong wished to repair the palace halls, Weixin remonstrated to the utmost; on this occasion he spoke of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall; the emperor started and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong wished to rebuild the palace, Weixin remonstrated fiercely, invoking the example of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall. The emperor started and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 同判睦親府內族撒合輦交結中外，久在禁近。

translations.literal: Associate Administrator of the Muxin Princely Establishment, inner clansman Sagelian, cultivated connections inside and outside, and had long been near the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Sagelian of the inner clan, Associate of the Muxin Princely Establishment, cultivated connections throughout the court and had long served near the throne.

sentences.zh: 哀宗為太子，有定策功，由是頗惑其言，複倚信日深，台諫每以為言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, Sagelian had merit in settling the succession; thereby he was much swayed by his words and again relied on him daily more deeply; the censorate and remonstrance bureau often spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong was crown prince, Sagelian had helped settle the succession; the emperor was much swayed by him and relied on him ever more deeply, though the censorate repeatedly protested.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗戒敕曰：「上之騎鞠舉樂，皆汝教之，再犯必杖汝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager once admonished: 'The emperor's cuju and music-making—all taught by you; if you offend again you will surely be beaten.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager once warned him, 'The emperor's cuju and revelry—you taught him all of it. Offend again and you will be beaten.'

sentences.zh: 」哀宗終不能去。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong in the end could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Emperor Aizong could not remove him.

sentences.zh: 尉忻諫曰：「撒合輦奸諛之最，日在天子左右，非社稷福。

translations.literal: Weixin remonstrated: 'Sagelian is the worst of flatterers and sycophants; daily at the Son of Heaven's side—no blessing to the altars of soil and grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Weixin remonstrated, 'Sagelian is the worst of flatterers, ever at the emperor's side—no blessing to the state.'

sentences.zh: 」上悔悟，出為中京留守，朝論快之。

translations.literal: The emperor repented and understood; he was sent out as Protector of the Central Capital; court opinion rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his senses and posted Sagelian as Protector of the Central Capital, to the satisfaction of court opinion.

sentences.zh: 五年，致仕，居汴中，崔立之變明日，召家人付以後事，望睢陽慟哭，以弓弦自縊而死，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he retired from office and lived in Bian; the day after Cui Li's mutiny he summoned his family, entrusted them with his final affairs, looked toward Suiyang and wailed bitterly, and hanged himself with a bowstring; he was then sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he retired and lived in Bianjing. The day after Cui Li's mutiny he summoned his family, settled his affairs, gazed toward Suiyang and wept bitterly, then hanged himself with a bowstring. He was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 一子名董七，沒於兵間。

translations.literal: One son named Dongqi perished amid the warfare.
translations.idiomatic: One son, named Dongqi, perished in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 弟秉甫，字正之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bingfu, courtesy name Zhengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bingfu, whose courtesy name was Zhengzhi.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：聶天驥素履清慎，赤盞尉忻天資忠諒，在治世皆足為良臣，不幸仕亂離之朝，以得死為願欲，哀哉！

translations.literal: The comment says: Nie Tianji in his conduct was pure and cautious; Chizhan Weixin by nature was loyal and sincere—in an age of good order both would suffice as fine ministers; unhappily they served a court of disorder and separation, and took death as their wish—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Nie Tianji lived with purity and caution; Chizhan Weixin was loyal and sincere by nature—in peaceful times both would have been fine ministers. Unhappily they served a dynasty in collapse and welcomed death as a release. How lamentable!
